newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Nov 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Nov 5.

text.p: THE DOMINION

A man accused of an "execution-style" murder has been freed on bail by a High Court judge, sparking an angry reaction from police. The bail ruling came two days after another man admitted murdering Kumeu teenager Nicola Rankin while out on bail on other serious charges. Page 1.

The Government has set up a $563,000 fund for political parties involved in coalition talks, apparently after prompting from NZ First. ACT NZ leader Richard Prebble made public on Monday a letter to party leaders from Finance Minister Bill

Birch that said negotiations were "placing heavy demands on at least one of the parties" taking part in coalition talks. Birch confirmed later the Government had agreed to set up the fund after a request from one of the parties. Page 1.
Radio Pacific bosses have warned former Cabinet minister John Banks to tone down provocative comments for his new breakfast show. Page 1.
The courts have no discretion to put Maori law, customs and values above statutes Parliament has enacted, the Court of Appeal has decided. Page 1.

Australia's controversial independent MP Pauline Hanson has been invited to speak at public meetings in New Zealand. The Auckland-based Government Accountability League, which has had several run-ins with the Race Relations Office, extended the invitation this week. Page 2.

New Zealand could be at the cutting edge of global telecommunications as the result of a merger between British Telecom and American long-distance carrier MCI, Clear Communications chief executive Andrew Makin said on Monday. The two companies are each 25 percent shareholders in Clear. When they merge to form Concert their shareholdings will give the new entity a half-share in Clear. Makin said the merger would take 18 months and in the interim Clear would have BT and MCI representatives on the board. Page 10.

Brierley Investments' share price could take another hit if Thistle Hotels' share price fell in London this week, analysts said on Monday. Under the British sharemarket rules, the lead broker of the float Merrill Lynch can support a share price for 30 days after listing, but that time ran out on Monday night. A failure by Merrill Lynch to keep Thistle above its 170 pence (395 cents) listing level has raised fears of a further price slump. Page 10.
The future of the $130 million EnergyDirect Community Trust is up for debate and the options include returning cash to customers of the former EnergyDirect power company. Page 10.

Computer software pirates in New Zealand got off with lenient fines because of "a certain degree of protectionism" by judges, Business Software Alliance vice-president Ron Eckstrom said on Monday. Page 10.
Disgruntled Southern Cross members were defeated on Monday in their bid to elect an outsider to the board of directors of the health insurance giant. Page 10.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Former Cabinet minister John Banks was pleased with himself on Monday after publicly sacking a journalist without warning in his first day on "truth radio". "I never in my wildest dreams thought I would be in a position to sack a news media hack, but I did today. I sacked Barry Soper," Banks said on Radio Pacific's breakfast show.
The caretaker Government on Monday created a special half-million-dollar fund from the public purse to meet the costs of the three parties involved in the coalition talks.

Evan Davis has been given a big incentive to keep the gambling tables at Sky City working hard. Under a proposed executive share option scheme, to be voted on at next month's annual meeting, the casino's managing director will be issued shares valued as much as $1.66 million by the year 2000. An appraisal by Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu judges the plan to be fair
and reasonable.
The merger of British Telecom with MCI Communication will have little effect in the short term on Clear Communications' competitive position chief executive Andrew Makin said on Monday.

Labour market data due for release this month and the Government's fiscal policy hold the key to any easing in monetary conditions by the Reserve Bank, according to Bankers Trust. It said a resolution to the political situation would provide direction for the market and the Reserve Bank but labour
market data due this month could also prove critical to the chances of an easing.
Prices on the new electricity market have again spiked to unusually high levels, prompting market operator EMCO to investigate.
Disruptions from industrial action and volcanic activity, and slower-than-forecast revenue growth, contributed to the Airways Corporation's below-budget performance in the June year, it says.
